Q: How do I detect the user's locale to get the correct csv separator? A:

This if real fun: CultureInfo.InstalledUICulture should be used for the recipient host. In your case that would be de I presume. Or de-GE.

I'm still stratching my head thinking what this should be called in UI, due to that the functionality won't be exposed to the external users.

Fun twist circa 2025: Win11 allows to customize list separator https://www.supportyourtech.com/tech/how-to-change-the-windows-11-list-separator-a-step-by-step-guide/ so now you have to go in to check with the recipient of CSV file if they did that and ponder if you adjust your code accordingly.

I wonder if life can be made any simpler using TSVs in place of CSVs. UPD: No it does not, Excel in win11 does not open tab separated files properly.

Q: OCR in Jira, how to get text information from screenshots A:

Native Jira Cloud currently doesn't support OCR on attachments. As far as I have checked also Rovo still can't "read" images - https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/ROVO-128. Most third-party solutions handle this by sending image data to external cloud APIs (like Azure AI or AWS Textract) for processing.

If data privacy is a concern (e.g., you don't want screenshots leaving the browser), I recently implemented a solution using Tesseract.js running via WebAssembly (WASM) directly within the Atlassian Forge platform. This performs the OCR client-side, so no data is sent to external AI services.

This functionality is available in my app Attachment Architect. It opens a side panel in the preview where you can copy logs/text directly.

[Disclaimer: I am the developer of Attachment Architect]

Q: GIT submodule active state is not working properly A:

I've never switched off submodules so I can only answer from documentation. AFAIU submodule.<name>.active and submodule.active are configuration values from .git/config, not from .gitmodules. submodule.<name>.active is a boolean that turns on/off the named submodule. submodule.active is a list of paths to active submodules. I.e. you can either do

git config submodule.my_doc_module.active false

to turn one submodule off or

git config --add submodule.active path1/to/module1
git config --add submodule.active path2/to/module2

to list only active submodules. After that run git submodule update --init --recursive.

See the docs for git submodule init and git config submodule.<name>.active.

BTW, .gitmodules doesn't have attribute active.

Q: PDF Precise checking location letters with different ascents and descents A:

I am using SlapKit but it's compatible with PdfPig so it should be the same.

Even using Letter, start and end baseline's won't be enough if you want to get precise with ascent's and descent's. You will have to go for the Letter's GlyphRectangle part. I just went with fontsize: 6 and line height: 6 because you didn't say what were your sizes.

Q: Git: Recover deleted (remote) branch A:

If the branch was deleted from GitHub using the delete branch button, then you can follow these steps:

  1. Go to the GitHub repo from which the branch was deleted.

  2. There will be an activity tab at the right menu bar in the About section of the repo. Click on it.

  3. It shows the activity that has happened on the current branch. On the branch name dropdown in the top left, click the View activity of all branches option.

  4. Now all the changes that you have done will be visible. Identify the branch that you have deleted.

  5. There will be a three dot(...) option saying more activity options. Click on it and click Restore branches option.

This might be able to restore the branch that you have just deleted. This will only work if the branch was deleted recently and it was deleted using GitHub and not Git. Check this answer for more info.
